title: Joshua 19:49–51
context: Once all the tribes have received their portions, the children of Israel give Joshua an inheritance of his own: the city of Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim, which he asked for according to the LORD’s commandment. Joshua, who with Caleb had been promised entry into the land (Numbers 14:30), receives his share last, after the people. The chapter closes by naming Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the tribal heads as those who distributed the land by lot at Shiloh before the LORD. Arminian and Reformed readers commonly treat this as shared ground: God keeps his word to faithful servants, leaders serve before they receive, and the whole distribution is carried out in God’s presence. Hebrews 4:8 reminds readers that the rest Joshua gave pointed beyond itself.

verses.text: So they finished distributing the land for inheritance by its borders. The children of Israel gave an inheritance to Joshua the son of Nun among them.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers note that the people finish distributing the land and then give Joshua an inheritance among them. The leader receives his portion only after the people have theirs.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see Joshua’s servant leadership in waiting until the end to receive his inheritance. Both traditions commonly see the verse as a model of leaders putting others first.

verses.text: According to the LORD’s commandment, they gave him the city which he asked, even Timnathserah in the hill country of Ephraim; and he built the city, and lived there.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers see Joshua receiving Timnathserah according to the LORD’s commandment, the city he asked for. God honors faithful servants, and Joshua builds and lives in his inheritance (compare Joshua 24:30).
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the fulfillment of God’s promise to Joshua, who with Caleb was promised entry into the land (Numbers 14:30). Readers in both traditions commonly treat the verse as shared ground on God’s faithfulness to his word.

verses.text: These are the inheritances, which Eleazar the priest, Joshua the son of Nun, and the heads of the fathers’ houses of the tribes of the children of Israel, distributed for inheritance by lot in Shiloh before the LORD, at the door of the Tent of Meeting. So they finished dividing the land.
verses.arminianNotes: Arminian readers note that the land was distributed by lot at Shiloh before the LORD, at the door of the Tent of Meeting. The whole process was carried out in God’s presence and under his authority.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the involvement of Eleazar, Joshua and the tribal heads as reflecting God’s ordered leadership (compare Joshua 14:1). Both traditions commonly see the completion of the allotment as testimony that God keeps his promises (compare Joshua 21:45).
